text:
It is truly a marvel of modern engineering that we have convinced ourselves that the secret to a sculpted physique lies not in actual exertion, but in the vigorous, rhythmic shaking of a piece of molded plastic. One can only imagine the sheer physical toll of those ten minutes of wrist-flicking; surely, the sheer intensity of such a workout must be equivalent to lifting a small mountain, or at the very least, moving a heavy sofa. The idea that one can bypass the tedious, sweaty reality of actual muscle building in favor of a few seconds of performative effort is the pinnacle of human laziness, wrapped in a shiny, colorful package.

As for my dental hygiene, I find that the most efficient and satirically appropriate tool for cleaning my teeth is a small, electric toothbrush. It vibrates with a precision that mocks the inefficiency of manual scrubbing, much like the plastic dumbbell mocks the concept of actual labor.
